summary: Pimaga Airport is a small regional airstrip serving the community of Pimaga in the Southern Highlands Province of Papua New Guinea. Situated in rugged, mountainous terrain at an elevation typical of the region, it functions primarily as a vital link for remote area access, missionary flights, and occasional charter services. The airport plays an important role in connecting isolated highland communities to larger population centers in the country.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft typically use Pimaga Airport?
A: Small turboprop aircraft and STOL (Short Take-Off and Landing) capable planes are the most common visitors, suited to the short runway and surrounding terrain.

Q: Is Pimaga Airport served by scheduled commercial flights?
A: Scheduled service is limited or infrequent; most flights are chartered or operated by missionary and aid organizations serving the region.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small rural airstrip, facilities are minimal, typically consisting of a basic terminal area and limited ground services.

Q: Are there any hazards pilots should be aware of?
A: The surrounding mountainous highland terrain requires careful approach and departure planning, and weather conditions can change rapidly in the region.
transport_tips: Ground transport options from Pimaga Airport are very limited, so arranging a vehicle in advance through local contacts or mission stations is strongly recommended. The airport is connected to the local road network, though travel times can be long due to the challenging highland terrain. Walking or using local transport may be the only options if no prior arrangement has been made.
local_tip: Bring cash in small denominations, as there are no ATMs or card facilities nearby, and local shops and transport services typically operate on a cash-only basis.
